headline: Every bite you eat was once alive—plants, animals, fungi—transformed into food
universal_truth: We are connected to all life through what we consume; eating is participating in nature's cycles
fun_facts: The average meal travels over 1,500 miles from farm to plate in developed countries
Most of the world's food comes from just 12 plant species and 5 animal species
A single ear of corn has about 800 kernels—each one capable of growing a new plant
discussion_questions: How connected do you feel to the sources of your food?
What would change if you grew or raised some of your own food?
Why have we become so disconnected from food production?

hook.script: That sandwich on your plate? The bread was wheat growing in a field. The lettuce was leaves absorbing sunlight. The meat was a living animal. Every bite you eat was alive—plants or animals transformed through farming, processing, and cooking into food.

cliff.script: Modern people rarely see food grow or animals raised. We buy packaged products with little connection to their origins. What happened between the living organism and your plate?
cliff.prompt: What transforms living things into food?

options.text: Farming, harvesting, processing, transportation, and preparation—a long chain from life to plate
options.response: Yes. Food systems are complex chains involving many steps and people. Each meal represents the work of farmers, processors, transporters, and cooks.

options.text: Factories process raw materials into the products we recognize as food
options.response: Processing is one step, but the chain starts much earlier—with living things growing...

fact1.title: Miles to Your Mouth
fact1.script: The average American meal travels over 1,500 miles from farm to plate. Apples from New Zealand, fish from Norway, spices from India. Your dinner represents a global network—impressive in scale, invisible in experience.

fact2.title: Narrow Diet
fact2.script: Despite thousands of edible plants, most of the world's food comes from just 12 plant species: wheat, corn, rice, potatoes, and a few others. Five animal species provide most meat. Our food system is remarkably concentrated.

fact3.title: Alive Until Eaten
fact3.script: Many foods remain alive until we eat them. Fruits and vegetables respire on your counter. Seeds in your bread could still sprout. The line between 'living thing' and 'food' is blurry—and recent.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Eating is participating in nature's cycles. Every meal connects you to farms, ecosystems, and other living things. Understanding where food comes from changes how you think about what you eat.

outro.script: That's Day 133. Tomorrow, we'll explore how farming changed everything. Until then, at your next meal, consider the journey each ingredient took to reach your plate.

growTrack.title: Food Origin Tracing - Follow the Chain
growTrack.activity: Pick one item from your next meal and trace its origin as far as you can. Where was it grown? How far did it travel? Who touched it along the way? This simple exercise reveals the invisible systems that feed you.
